title: Ethel Waters, Florence Mills and others visiting the Nest
summary: He recalls Ethel Waters and Earl Dancer's quarrel, Florence Mills sitting at a table, and how Mills got her break replacing Gertie Saunders.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And it was a great place. Ethel Waters was there. She was with Earl Dancer there, I remember on one occasion. We had a big party there, about fifteen or eighteen of us. And it was Ethel Waters' turn and Earl Dancer HAD said to buy her a drink. And as soon as they'd turn around to buy a drink, they'd start fussin' amongst on to themselves and broke up the party and went on out and didn't pay the check.
Well did -- when people like Ethel Waters came in, performers, would they sometimes get up and perform, or would they just drink?

Oh, yeah. But Florence Mills never got up. But Florence Mills sat at the table. I'll never forget her. That's the only song I ever played for her. Ethel Waters wasn't as big as she was later on. She was just being made. She had played the Palace. And Earl Dancer was a sort of manager and boy friend, and husband, whatever we called it then. But she hadn't arrived yet, see?
In fact, very few of us had arrived at

that time. Edith Wilson used to be there. Florence Mills was about the only one that had actually arrived. And she arrived because on account of the ignorance of Gertie Saunders. When Gertie Saunders walked out of "Shuffle Along", Florence Mills stepped in and that made her.
